class TeachingScene(Scene):

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: Snell’s Law", [
            "Refractive index defines how light slows.",
            "Snell's law relates angles and indices.",
            "Notice the normal line and angles.",
            "Light bends when moving between media.",
            "Adjust the angle to see refraction shift."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        snells_law = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin(\theta_1) = n_2 \sin(\theta_2)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(snells_law, "B3", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(snells_law))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Setup Diagram elements
        boundary = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D6"], color=WHITE)
        normal = DashedLine(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F4"], color=GRAY)
        
        # Incident Ray
        incident_ray = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["D4"], color=WHITE)
        incident_angle_label = Text("Angle of Incidence", color="#FFFF00", font_size=16)
        self.place_at_grid(incident_angle_label, "C2")
        
        self.play(Create(boundary), Create(normal), Create(incident_ray), Write(incident_angle_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Refracted Ray
        refracted_ray = Line(self.grid["D4"], self.grid["F5"], color=WHITE)
        refracted_angle_label = Text("Angle of Refraction", color="#00FF00", font_size=16)
        self.place_at_grid(refracted_angle_label, "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(refracted_ray), Write(refracted_angle_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#AAAAAA")
        self.play(Indicate(snells_law))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF8800")
        
        # Simple dynamic simulation
        theta1 = ValueTracker(PI/4)
        
        # Update logic
        def update_ray(m):
            angle = theta1.get_value()
            m.put_start_and_end_on(
                self.grid["D4"] + np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0]) * 1.5,
                self.grid["D4"]
            )
            
        incident_ray.add_updater(update_ray)
        self.play(theta1.animate.set_value(PI/3), run_time=2)
        incident_ray.remove_updater(update_ray)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Physics of Refraction: Why Light Bends

sections.title: The Hook: The Broken Pencil Illusion
sections.content: Introduce the phenomenon by showing a pencil in a half-full glass of water. Explain that light changes direction when moving between media, creating a visual 'break'.
sections.example: An animation of a pencil submerged in water; the submerged portion appears shifted upward due to light rays bending at the air-water interface.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly define light as a wave with speed (v), frequency (f), and wavelength (λ). Establish that light travels fastest in a vacuum and slows down in denser materials (optical density).
sections.example: Visual metaphor: A marching band moving from smooth pavement (fast) to thick mud (slow) at an angle, causing the rows to rotate/turn.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Snell’s Law
sections.content: Define the Refractive Index (n = c/v). Present Snell's Law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2). Use a diagram showing the 'Normal' line, the Angle of Incidence (θ1), and the Angle of Refraction (θ2).
sections.example: An interactive animation overlay: Adjusting the laser angle (θ1) shows the refracted beam (θ2) responding in real-time according to the calculated index of refraction.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Archer Fish
sections.content: Apply the concept to nature. Explain how an Archer Fish compensates for refraction when spitting water at insects above the surface by aiming 'below' where the prey appears to be.
sections.example: A side-profile animation showing the fish 'calculating' the refraction shift to successfully hit a beetle perched on an overhanging branch.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Summarize that refraction occurs due to a change in speed when entering a new medium. Reiterate that light bends toward the normal when slowing down, and away when speeding up.
sections.example: A quick-fire graphical summary: Light entering glass (fast to slow, bends toward normal) vs. light exiting glass (slow to fast, bends away from normal).
